ogTitle: Koh Samui 3 Days 2 Nights — Beaches, Big Buddha & Ang Thong
ogDesc: A Samui trip paced just right — beaches and Big Buddha on day one, a southern loop on day two, Ang Thong on day three, with real ballpark costs and honest warnings.
intro: Koh Samui packs pretty beaches, striking temples and the limestone seascape of Ang Thong Marine Park into one island. The catch is that three days is just short enough to mess up your route and end up driving the whole trip. So this plan keeps it simple: day one eases you in around the north of the island with beach time, day two loops the south for temples and waterfalls, and day three is Ang Thong all day. The idea is less time on the road, more time actually seeing things, and enough room to genuinely sit by the sea — not just snap a photo and move on.

blocks.html: Before the plan, a straight word about time. Koh Samui is bigger than people expect — the ring road (Route 4169) runs about 50 km around the island and takes the better part of an hour if you keep stopping. So the trick is simple: don't hop back and forth across the island in a single day. Whatever zone you're in, finish it before moving on, and you'll save a lot of energy. The plan below is already grouped by zone.

items: Day 1 — north and east: check in around Chaweng or Bophut, swim at Chaweng Beach, visit the Big Buddha in the evening, then wrap up at Fisherman's Village in Bophut
Day 2 — southern loop: Hin Ta–Hin Yai rocks, Na Muang Waterfall, Wat Khunaram to see the mummified monk, then a swim at Lamai Beach
Day 3 — Ang Thong Marine Park: a full-day boat tour with snorkelling, kayaking and the inner-sea viewpoint, then back to rest before your flight home
Adjust to your flights — if you land late on day one, just swap days 1 and 2. Keep the Ang Thong day for whenever the weather looks calmest.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Chaweng Beach + Big Buddha + Bophut

blocks.html: Keep day one easy — no rushing — since most flights land at Samui airport mid-morning anyway. The Chaweng–Bophut–Bang Rak zone is closest to the airport, so covering this area first makes the most sense.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Ease into the north — beach time and the Big Buddha

items.activity: Arrive at Samui airport, check in around Chaweng or Bophut
items.note: Staying in this zone saves travel time on your first and last days. The drive from the airport into Chaweng is about 10–15 min.

items.activity: Grab lunch around Chaweng, then hit Chaweng Beach
items.note: Chaweng is a white-sand stretch about 6 km long with clear water. From late morning into the afternoon the surf is gentle and good for swimming; come evening it turns into the island's party strip.

items.activity: Head back to your room to shower and rest a bit
items.note: The afternoon sun on Samui is strong. Duck out of it for a while and head out again in the evening — much more comfortable.

items.activity: Visit the Big Buddha at Wat Phra Yai (Koh Fan)
items.note: Open roughly 7am to 6–7pm, no entry fee. The 12-metre Buddha sits at the top of a naga staircase with views over Koh Phangan and Bophut Bay. Dress modestly, shoulders and knees covered.
The walking street is busiest every Friday from 5pm to 11pm, but seaside spots are open on other days too — sit down for seafood and watch the sunset.

items.activity: Seaside dinner in Bophut, then back to your room

blocks.title: About sun and surf on day one
blocks.html: Chaweng is an easy, shallow beach to swim at and good for kids. But during the monsoon (October–December) the surf can pick up and the water turns murkier than usual. Check the warning flags and ask your hotel before you go in, every time.

blocks.text: Day 2 — southern loop: rocks, temples, waterfalls, Lamai

blocks.html: Today you drive (or rent a scooter / hire a taxi) around the south, picking up the popular landmarks that sit almost all on the same road. Start at the Hin Ta–Hin Yai rocks, work your way to Wat Khunaram and the waterfall, then finish at Lamai Beach, which is quieter than Chaweng.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Temples, waterfalls and odd rocks, then a swim at Lamai

items.activity: Leave your hotel, head for the Hin Ta–Hin Yai rocks (end of Lamai Beach)
items.note: Oddly shaped rocks tied to a grandfather–grandmother legend. Free entry, with souvenir and snack stalls around. About 30–40 min for a walk and photos.

items.activity: On to Wat Khunaram to see the body of Luang Por Daeng (the mummified monk)
items.note: On Route 4169 between Na Muang and Hua Thanon. Free to enter (donate as you wish). It's the preserved, still-seated body of a monk who has not decayed since the 1970s. Dress modestly and remove your shoes before entering.

Na Muang 1 is an easy walk from the car park, with a pool you can swim in. Na Muang 2 needs more of a hike up. In the rainy season there's plenty of water but the rocks get slippery — watch your footing.

items.activity: Lunch around Lamai or Hua Thanon
items.note: The Hua Thanon area has a market and local southern-Thai and seafood spots at friendly prices.
Lamai is quieter and wider than Chaweng, with clear water — good for swimming and lazing around. There are beach clubs and seaside bars to settle into for a while.

items.activity: Catch the sunset and have dinner on Lamai Beach

blocks.title: Riding a scooter on Samui — be careful
blocks.html: Scooter rental runs roughly 250–1,000 THB a day depending on the model, and it's the easiest way to loop the island. But some stretches — especially the climbs to the viewpoints and the road into the waterfall — are steep and slippery. Ride slow, wear a helmet, and if you're not genuinely comfortable on a scooter, a hired taxi or the local songthaew (pickup truck) is the safer call.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Ang Thong Marine National Park

blocks.html: This is the highlight of the trip: a limestone seascape of nearly 42 islands, with the inner sea (an emerald-green lagoon inside the main island), snorkelling spots and kayaking. You can only reach it by boat — tours leave Samui in the morning and return in the late afternoon. Book ahead and save this day for whenever the weather looks calmest on your trip.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: A full-day boat tour at Ang Thong

items.activity: Tour van picks you up from your hotel, off to the pier
items.note: Most tours include free hotel pickup and drop-off. Confirm the meeting point and time with your operator the night before.

items.activity: Set off by boat to the Ang Thong islands
items.note: A speedboat takes about 45 min to an hour from Samui; a larger boat is slower but steadier. Choose based on how easily you get seasick.

items.activity: Snorkel and kayak around the islands
items.note: Most tours provide snorkelling gear and kayaks. The water is clear enough to see coral and schools of fish. Keep your life jacket on and listen to the guide about the currents.

items.activity: Go ashore for a buffet lunch on Wua Talap island
items.note: Standard tours include a buffet lunch.

items.activity: Climb up to the inner-sea viewpoint (the Emerald Lagoon)
items.note: The climb to the viewpoint is fairly steep and hot — wear trainers and bring water. If you're not up for it, you can relax on the beach below.

items.activity: Pack up, board the boat and head back to Samui
Back at your hotel — shower, rest, pack
items.note: If you fly out the next day, tonight's a good time for one last easy seafood dinner.

blocks.title: Ang Thong depends on the weather — straight talk
blocks.html: During the monsoon (late October–December) the sea on this side gets rough, and on some days the park closes or tours are cancelled for safety. If you're coming in the rainy season, leave a spare day and pick a tour that refunds if it's cancelled due to weather. Park entry fees for Thais and foreigners are charged separately and usually paid on top of the tour price.

Prices on the island swing hard with the season — in high season (December–April) both rooms and tours can roughly double. The figures below are mid-range numbers to set a budget by; check the real prices for your travel dates.

items: Accommodation, 2 nights: a mid-range guesthouse or hotel runs around 800–2,500 THB/night · beachfront resorts go several times higher
Ang Thong tour: a speedboat tour is around 1,700–2,500 THB/person including transfers, food and gear · larger boats are cheaper, from the high hundreds to low thousands of THB
Ang Thong park entry: usually paid separately at the park (foreigners 300 THB, children 150 THB, Thais cheaper)
Transport: scooter rental around 250–1,000 THB/day · songthaew 50–200 THB/trip · a private taxi is a matter of negotiation, usually starting from 300 THB
Temples and landmarks: the Big Buddha, Hin Ta–Hin Yai and Wat Khunaram are free or donation-based · Na Muang Waterfall is free

blocks.text: A few things before you go

items: Book the Ang Thong tour ahead — especially in high season, when boats fill fast and prices climb
Carry cash — small shops, markets and several park entry points take cash first
Sunscreen and a hat — the Samui sun is strong all day, especially on the boat day
Modest clothes for temples — shoulders and knees covered; a scarf in your bag is the easiest fix
Check the forecast before any water activity — safety comes before the view

faq.q: Is 3 days and 2 nights enough for Koh Samui?
faq.a: It's enough to cover the main highlights — beach time, the Big Buddha, the southern temple-and-waterfall loop, and one day at Ang Thong Marine Park. If you also want to add Koh Phangan or scuba diving, allow 4 days and 3 nights to do it comfortably.

faq.q: Which area of Samui should I stay in for a short trip?
faq.a: Chaweng, or Bophut–Bang Rak, is the most convenient — close to the airport, the beaches, the Big Buddha and Fisherman's Village, which keeps travel short on your first and last days.

faq.q: Which day of the trip should I do Ang Thong?
faq.a: Pick whichever day the forecast looks calmest, since it's a water activity that depends on the wind and waves. During the late-year monsoon some tours are cancelled for safety, so leave a spare day and choose a tour that refunds cancellations.

faq.q: Can I get around the island without riding a scooter?
faq.a: Yes. Use the songthaew (50–200 THB/trip) or hire a taxi or van by the day, and you can still cover all the landmarks. It's safer if you're not used to the island's steep roads. Agree the price before you get in, every time.

faq.q: Is the Samui Big Buddha free, and what are the hours?
faq.a: It's free, open roughly 7am to 6–7pm daily. Go in the morning or evening to avoid the heat and get nicer photos. Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered.
